utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, good afternoon. Are you hearing me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If I understand him well, he's got the French version. Could you put it on -- the Serbo-Croat would be number what? Is it all right now? Are you hearing me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-94-2-PT, the Prosecutor versus Dragan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: May it please, Your Honour, Upawansa Yapa appearing for the Prosecution. With me is Patricia Sellers and Mr. William Smith. MS. Diane Boles is the case manager for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you. Appearances for the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Howard Morrison for Dragan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you. Let's go straight to the most important part of our agenda for today's meeting. You will recall that following a motion by the Prosecution for leave to amend the first amended indictment, a long-awaited motion, I must say, this Chamber on the 15th of February of this year, filed its decision, and as a result of which, we now have a second amended indictment, an indictment which -- an amended indictment which essentially reduces the original 80 counts to eight counts, but with some changes that are significant. I'm referring in particular to the fact that this second amended indictment adds three new charges under Counts 2, 3 and 6, which naturally necessitate the -- that your client, Mr. Morrison, enters a new plea. Now, before proceeding any further, I just wanted to make sure that your client is -- has already been made aware of the nature of the amendments effected to the indictment and particularly as to the nature of the changes that have been effected. If that is not the case, or if your client thinks that this Trial Chamber ought to give -- explain to him the nature of these changes in some detail, then naturally I am prepared to go ahead and I will give a short explanation. But I would await for a response from you first, before embarking into that, Mr. Morrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the amended indictment has been served upon my client in a language he understands. He's had the opportunity to read it. I've had the opportunity to go through it with him. I do not think it is necessary for him to have anything else done today other than simply be arraigned as to what his plea is on those fresh matters. He will immediately correct me, I'm sure, if I'm wrong as to that assumption, but these are matters to which he has already indicated the nature of the plea and I have already indicated to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Morrison. And also another point that I would like to raise is that your client has a right to have either the entire new amended indictment or the amended parts of the indictment or the newly introduced parts in the indictment read out to him in a language that he can understand. Does he insist on this right, or does he opt to renounce to it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the investigation has already been made into that, and Mr. Nikolic is content that simply the new amended parts are put to him. He doesn't require repetition of those matters which have already been, as it were, arraigned, and he doesn't require the full details to be put to him. I've discussed this already with my learned friends from the OTP and indeed with the learned associate, and it can be done in short form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So basically, if I read you well, you would agree if the Chamber just informs for formality's sake that -- your client that three new charges have been brought against him under counts 2, 3, and 6 and then proceed to ask him to enter a plea, either to those three particular counts, amended counts, or to -- just a general plea to the whole amended indictment, whichever one you as Defence counsel prefers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the -- a plea to -- a general plea to the amended indictment will suffice because it will be the same plea, even if it was put on individual counts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Okay. Mr. Morrison we can proceed along these lines. The Trial Chamber is informing you that the new indictment Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. contains three new charges against you which are contained in counts 2, 3, and 6. Basically, count 2 charges inhumane acts allegedly to have taken place in the Susica camp as a crime against humanity. Count 3 charges you with an additional murder, namely that relating to the killing of a certain Galib Music. And count 6 alleges torture as a crime against humanity in particular and relation to two individuals, namely say Sead Ambeskovic, and Hajrudin Osmanovic. That said, the only other thing remaining to me is to ask you what plea you want to enter to the second amended indictment, as I understand you are aware of it. Do you plead guilty or not guilty according to the second amended indictment? Unless you want to state something else, in which case you are free to go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to plea. I have nothing else to say except that I plead not guilty, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Nikolic. You may sit down. Mr. Morrison, is there anything else you would like to state in regard to this particular stage, part of our agenda?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Your Honour, no. It is plain that those are now all matters which are in issue between the Prosecution and the Defence. Your Honour may not be aware that since the last hearing, there has been significant new disclosure under Rule 66 and Rule 68 in respect of the Defence. There are included in that disclosure a total of 58 statements which have not yet been translated into B/C/S, and therefore I cannot take instructions from Mr. Nikolic. I'm informed that the time scale, because of the pressure of work for such translations, is going to be in the order of four to six weeks from today, which means that it's going to be difficult to take the matter further before, first of all, Mr. Nikolic has had the opportunity to read and absorb the new statements and, secondly, for him to give me detailed instructions upon them. As soon as that's been done - which looks from the time scale point of view to be no earlier than the end of April of this year - I will be in a position to enter into hopefully some meaningful discussions with the Prosecution as to the future conduct of this case. I can start that process in respect of those statements which have already been translated and in respect of which I already have instructions, but I'm not evidently going to be able to finish that process until the statements are available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand that. And I appreciate you putting the Chamber into the picture. Mr. Yapa, is there any way in which this process could be hastened?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know what the difficulties are, and I know that you are not answerable and you cannot account for these problems, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: I'm thankful to Your Honour for raising this question. We have had some consultation, and the understanding we have is that it will take four to five weeks for the translations to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How bulky are these documents? How voluminous?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are about 20 new statements. It's only that much. But the time given is four to five weeks for the translations to take place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. We'll move to the next item on our agenda for this -- for today's meeting, this afternoon's meeting, and that is the pending motion on the illegality of the arrest. Now, I'm afraid, Mr. Morrison, that I am not a harbourer of good news today in this regard because the situation is not much changed since the last meeting. What I can explain is that we've had some problems, human resources problems, as a result of which progress in the elaboration of the decision on the -- on your motion on the alleged illegality of your client's arrest has been -- has had to slow down. We should be in a position to proceed at a faster speed now that we have got an additional officer present now, recruited, and it should make it possible for the legal officer who was working on this motion, on the research involved on this motion, to concentrate more on this matter. However, I do want to make myself clear on this. It's not something that has been abandoned or something that has been neglected. It's something that we are working upon. We consider it of the utmost importance, being -- regarding an alleged illegal arrest, and I can assure you that it will receive our utmost attention. But we require more time, and we will keep you informed, and hopefully, by the next meeting, we will be in a position to hand down our decision, unless fresh problems arise. Do you have anything to state in regard?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Your Honour, no. Thank you for keeping the Defence apprised of the position. The situation is this, that we are inevitably delayed by the translation problems. Even if the motion was, as it were, ready today, that translation problem wouldn't have gone away so the time scale wouldn't, I would have thought, be much affected. Besides which, I always found it unwise to complain about any lapse of time for which I'm not responsible because when there comes a lapse of time for which I am responsible, it's much easier to make well-received motions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I appreciate that, Mr. Morrison. I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: It all depends how I phrase it on the next occasion as to how it's appreciated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we move to any other matter that you would like to raise. Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: We do not have any matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Your Honour, no, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, it is customary for this Trial Chamber, each time there is a meeting of this kind, to ensure that your state of health is good and it's being given attention to, and that the conditions pertaining to your state of detention in the detention centre of this Tribunal are adequate and according to recognised standards and also the rules of this Tribunal. Do you -- is there anything that you would like to state in regard to either of these two points that I have raised with you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no comments to make. My health is fine. Of course, now I've been here for a while, nearly two years, the personnel in the detention unit are well. I have no problems. I have visits from my family. Generally speaking, I have nothing to complain about. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Nikolic. I suppose there is nothing else to be added, and that being the case, the meeting is closed. We stand adjourned to the next one. Thank you. Incidentally, Mr. Morrison and Mr. Yapa, if, during -- between now and the next meeting, assuming that the translations would have been forwarded to you and there are discussions that may impact the need for us to proceed with the decision on the illegal arrest or the future of this trial, to please come forward in the usual, recognised manner and inform the Tribunal, the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.
